title: Jan-Willem Doornenbal, Riso Fort Zuid Wilgen
lede: A scan of an A3 three-color riso print of willows reflected in water, in blue, yellow, and black.
summary: Scan of a three-color A3 riso photo print in blue, yellow, and black.

source.label: Flickr: Jan-Willem Doornenbal, “Riso Fort Zuid Wilgen”

evidence.note: Viewed the 1024 × 726 px Flickr “large” file, a flatbed scan of the whole sheet, so the color is closer to the print than in a photograph.

styles.note: Three spot inks separate a photograph, with banding and grain from the drum.

context: The Flickr description says: “Scan van een 3-kleuren risoprint op A3-formaat. Blauw, geel en zwart.” (Scan of a three-color riso print in A3 format. Blue, yellow, and black.)
observed: The photograph is split into three inks: a mid blue for water, a pale yellow for the far bank, and black for branches.
Blue and yellow overlap into green in the trees at the left.
Large blue areas show fine horizontal banding and grain near the lower edge.
The image is printed with a wide white paper margin.
interpretation: Riso separations do not reproduce full color. They turn a photograph into a few flat, translucent layers.
borrow: Split an image into two or three ink layers with hard thresholds instead of a smooth full-color photo.

images.alt: A scanned print of willow branches reflected in water, in blue, pale yellow, and black, with a white margin.
